title: Round 38 New Jersey-Hawaii state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for New Jersey and Hawaii. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). High Point and Mauna Kea carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. The same-name disambiguations (Lake Hopatcong, Kailua, Wailuku River, Mauna Loa/Maunaloa), the Waiau name-order screen, the Delaware River's out-of-state keying, and the displaced Elizabeth/Kahului records are documented below.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. Same-name records of another county, class, or island, adjacent harbour/aqueduct records, historical records, and census-designated places were rejected explicitly where relevant. Hawaii names are stored verbatim, including macrons and ʻokina (Līhuʻe, Haleakalā); the extraction staging had to use those exact spellings because the DomesticNames matcher is literal.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for High Point (877098) and Mauna Kea (366215), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the summit elevations cite USGS-published values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-20; this register is the frozen batch-20 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (text class Reservoir for Lake Hopatcong, Round Valley Reservoir), Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor (the Delaware River under NJ; Candlewood Lake in batch 19).
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

knownLimitations: New Jersey and Hawaii are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by official name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so High Point (1,803 feet), Mauna Kea (13,796 feet), Mauna Loa (13,681 feet), and Haleakalā (10,023 feet) elevations cite USGS-published values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines; the Hawaii frame's ocean reaches are schematic.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. The Hawaii rectangle spans the main island chain from Hawaii to Kauai; Niʻihau and the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands carry no seeded rows. No boundary geometry is claimed.
